newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to help Alphatec after debt restructure.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to help Alphatec after debt restructure.

text.p: Thailand's government will step in to help cash-strapped electronics giant Alphatec Group once the firm finishes negotiating with creditors its debt restructuring, Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi said.
But he stressed in an interview with Reuters on Wednesday that he had thrown his weight behind the group which is at the front line of the domestic electronic industry
"We must help Alphatec. The company has around $1.0 billion a year worth of orders. We risk losing it to a neighbouring country if Alphatec collapses," he said.
"However, there is no use stepping in right now. The government wants to make sure that the group will have revolving credit facilities before pumping in money," he said.
Alphatec Group was hard hit by Thailand's economic slowdown and extremely bearish stock market. The company faced difficulties raising funds to finance its various project.

One of the biggest blows came last month when U.S.-based Texas Instruments Inc terminated two joint ventures with the group, citing difficult economic conditions in Thailand which affect Alphatec's major share holder and chairman Charn Uswachoke toraise finance.

The government, in a move to help Alphatec, suggested that the company move away repayment date, restructure debt with creditors, transform some of the loans into equity, and find new business partners.
Korn said he expected the company to be able to restructure the debt within 90 days.
"We will see then if there is a need to invest in Alphatec. If so, we will do it," he said, but declined to provide details.
